title: TSG vs RMP
summary: Arms / Unholy / Resto Druid into Sub Rogue, Frost Mage and Disc. The mirror of the RMP guide, written from the side that does not need a perfect go — and the first plan here where forcing their cooldowns is the whole win condition.

sections.title: You are not the setup team here — that changes what a failed go means
sections.body:
This comp has one long amplification and a lot of continuous damage. RMP has the opposite: little pressure between windows, and everything staked on assembling one.

So a go that forces their Ice Block and their Pain Suppression without killing anyone is a success for you and a failure for them, even though the same scoreboard shows nothing. Their answers are two-minute and three-minute; yours come back far sooner.

The corollary is the part players get wrong: do not spend your control creating a kill window you do not need. Most of it is worth more denying theirs.

sections.title: Kill target: the Mage, unless the Priest is already out of position
sections.body:
The Rogue holds six answers and two of them — Cloak of Shadows and Evasion — are near-total against exactly what this comp does. Cloak answers the Death Knight's magic damage and every silence; Evasion answers the Warrior. Training a Rogue through both is a way to spend a round achieving nothing.

The Mage holds four, and two of those (Ice Barrier, Greater Invisibility) do not survive real pressure. His long answer is Ice Block, and it is the one you are trying to spend.

The counter-argument, stated because it is not settled: the Mage is the hardest to pin and the Rogue is the one who has to stand still to kill you. Pressure on the Rogue may be worth more as peel-suppression than the kill on the Mage is worth as a kill.

steps.note: On the Priest the moment their go starts. A silenced healer cannot Pain Suppression, and this is the cheapest way to make their whole attempt worth nothing.
On the Rogue, not the Mage. It is free, and it takes the one player who must be in melee out of the window entirely.
Not control, but it belongs in this sequence: it is the answer to a Polymorph or a Blast and it comes back inside every cadence.

sections.title: Control the Priest when you do commit

steps.note: Stun first, so the follow-up lands on a healer who cannot act rather than one who can trinket on reaction.
Fresh category. The Druid can only hold one target in a Cyclone at a time, so this is a choice not to have the Rogue out.
Long cooldown for six seconds. GUESS: this may be worth more saved as a peel — it is the only thing here that can interrupt their go without a stun.
The comp's real gate. Everything else is scheduled around it.
Inside Avatar rather than on cooldown, since the two land on the same tier only every second attempt.
Summoned before the window, not during it — it is pressure that arrives, not damage you press.
Stun, so it survives your own damage — the only kind of control that belongs on the person you are killing.
Second stun, diminished if it follows Storm Bolt straight away. It is worth more on the next attempt.
Not control, and it will not stop a Blink — but it is free and it costs the Mage the reposition.
Two minutes. Forcing this is what a good go looks like when nobody dies.
Back every attempt, so it is not a cooldown you are spending — it is the floor.
Also drops threat and most damage over time. If he uses it early, his real answer is gone.

sections.title: What the Rogue answers with — the reason he is not the target

steps.note: Magic immunity: it answers the Death Knight almost entirely for its duration.
And the Warrior, separately. Two different answers to your two damage dealers.
Short, always up, and the reason chip damage on a Rogue accomplishes nothing.
Not a personal defensive so much as a way to make your go impossible to finish.

sections.title: Where this is guessing
sections.body:
1. Whether to commit at all before their Ice Block is gone. This plan says to pressure early and go late, but a Warrior sitting on Avatar while it comes back off cooldown is also wasting the comp's only real window.

2. The Cyclone allocation. It appears twice above, on different targets, and the Druid can only hold one person at a time. Which one actually wins the round is not something I can derive.

3. Intimidating Shout as a peel versus as part of a chain. Same trade as Blind in the mirror guide, and I could not settle it there either.

4. This whole plan assumes you out-sustain them if nobody dies. If RMP can reset and force a mana war instead, the assumption is backwards and the guide is wrong from the first paragraph.
